title: Summit Reserve Property Tax Refund Reviews: Horizon Where a Maturity or Payoff Case Is Open
content:
When the kept amount of a returned property tax refund is worked out for a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts, the horizon of the refund review follows the loan's end where the Summit loan's records already show one.

## Rule

- **Maturity case.** Where the reserve's Summit loan has a maturity case (Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases) that is due and payable, or in its extension period, and that case carries a resolution deadline, the horizon of the refund review is the whole months from the handling date to that resolution deadline, never below zero.
- **Payoff case.** Where it has no such maturity case and a payoff case (Payoff and Loan Satisfaction) on the loan has terms issued or accepted and carries a statement good-through date, the horizon of the refund review is the whole months from the handling date to that good-through date, never below zero.
- Where the loan has neither, this rule does not set the horizon.

Whole months are complete calendar months: a month counts only when the later date reaches the handling date's day number. A maturity case with no resolution deadline is not "such a maturity case", so a qualifying payoff case then decides.

## Decision table

| Maturity case due and payable or in extension, with a resolution deadline | Payoff case with terms issued or accepted, with a good-through date | Horizon |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes or no | Whole months to the resolution deadline |
| No | Yes | Whole months to the good-through date |
| No | No | Not set by this rule |

## Boundary cases on hypothetical dates (handling date 10 March)

| Date on the case | Whole months | Horizon |
|---|---|---|
| Resolution deadline 10 September | 6 | 6 |
| Resolution deadline 9 September | 5 | 5 |
| Good-through date 25 March, no qualifying maturity case | 0 | 0 |
| Resolution deadline 1 March, already passed | below zero | 0 |
